clue.text: Outrage results when lad returns to examine data

parts.note: to scan data is to examine it closely

indicators.note: the word lad comes back on itself, read from right to left

explanation.surface: Something shocking happens when a young man comes back to go over the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lad returns' comes first in the clue but ends the answer: 'returns' gives DAL, the young man turned round, placed after the scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public disgrace that provokes outrage, and the word also names the outrage itself.

clue.text: Bombarded by airmen in set formation by day

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other
a formation is an arrangement, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is Britain's body of airmen

explanation.surface: Airmen flying in formation pounded the target during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' is not the airmen flying in formation: it rearranges 'set' as STE, and the RAF goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Pay attention to speech

explanation.surface: Listen carefully to the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it; an address is also a formal speech.

clue.text: Writer takes a nip of whisky at first

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky
taken as written
first is written 1st, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An author begins by having a quick shot of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' seems to say 'initially' but gives AT plus 1ST, with 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a writer of plays.

clue.text: Stories about toddler? That's an understatement

indicators.note: the first piece goes about the second, enclosing it

parts.note: lies are stories, as in telling stories
a tot is a small child or toddler

explanation.surface: Someone telling tales about a small child is putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by denying the opposite, such as 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Moderate parties offer parity for all

parts.note: moderate, as in middling or reasonable, means fair
dos are parties or celebrations, as in a birthday do

explanation.surface: Centrist political parties promise equal treatment for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate parties' looks like a political phrase but gives FAIR and DOS. FAIR DOS is an informal British phrase asking for fair shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dos is a British colloquial call for equal treatment, everyone getting the same share.

clue.text: Finicky fellow causes stir over cannabis

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or fuss
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A fussy man makes a commotion about marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a person who worries over trivial details.

clue.text: Journal that is about to make an impression

indicators.note: the first piece is about, around, the second

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a mag, short for magazine, is a journal

explanation.surface: A periodical is set to make its mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture, an impression of something.

clue.text: Wanted resided elsewhere

indicators.note: elsewhere means in a different place, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone who was sought had lived somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired means longed for or sought after.

clue.text: Society milliner gets thoroughly upset

parts.note: a milliner makes hats, so a hatter

explanation.surface: A fashionable hat-maker becomes very distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shattered by news is to be devastated, deeply distressed.

clue.text: New plan to build revolutionary catamaran?

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, from the colour of left-wing revolution
a catamaran was originally a raft of logs lashed together, so a raft serves as an example

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a fresh design for building a radical twin-hulled boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the catamaran as only one kind of raft.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to draw up a document or scheme again, making a fresh version of it.

clue.text: Pens presented by each Welsh city

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
ea is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price labels

explanation.surface: Writing implements are handed over with each sale in a city in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' suggests writing tools but means female swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales.

clue.text: She fared badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman had a poor time of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a girl's name, so it can stand for a female pronoun.

clue.text: Ordered to respect what mustn't be divulged!

indicators.note: letters ordered are arranged afresh, so these two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: People told to show deference regarding confidential matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified information marked at the highest security level must never be revealed.

clue.text: Reject the young Persephone?

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the goddess in her girlhood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman myth Dis, god of the underworld, carried off Persephone, so as a girl she was Dis's miss, read together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss is to reject or send away; split as DIS MISS it is the underworld god's young woman.

clue.text: Ruth and Ned made a terrible noise

indicators.note: made means fashioned or built, so the two names are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Two people kicked up an awful racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two names and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The crash and rumble after lightning is the classic example of a frightening noise.

clue.text: Superior worker has the advantage

parts.note: upper means higher or superior
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A senior employee holds the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand means being in control, holding the advantage.

clue.text: Detailed to appear in court again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a person cited is summoned to appear before a court

explanation.surface: Someone has been told to turn up before the judge a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to list or enumerate items in turn, much as one details them.

clue.text: Ridiculing a knitter's work

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing is good-natured teasing; it is also the ridged pattern of knit-and-purl stitches.

clue.text: Risk getting, left behind in church

indicators.note: one piece comes behind, after, the other

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble on being abandoned at the service.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, kept for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Draughtsmen's bloomers

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by technical illustrators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests blunders but means old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers are people who draw, like draughtsmen; drawers are also knickers, as are bloomers.

clue.text: Check made about journalists

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: An inspection is carried out on the reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or hold back, keeping a feeling or movement in check.

clue.text: Terribly ill, dear, but now recovered

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone was very unwell but is now on the mend.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to regain strength after illness.

clue.text: Malevolent look upset animated onlooker

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: live means lively or animated
an eye is something that looks on

explanation.surface: A spiteful glance disturbed a lively spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a glare believed to bring harm to its target.

clue.text: Hat? Leave it, lad!

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone tells a boy not to touch a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a broad-brimmed cowboy hat.

clue.text: Boycott by postal service may constitute it

definitions.text: Boycott by postal service may constitute it

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, a trade-union usage
the mail is the postal service

explanation.surface: A postal workers' refusal to handle certain items amounts to extortion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points to the answer: a postal union blacking the mail could amount to holding people to ransom.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is extortion by threat, and a boycott used to force concessions can amount to that.

clue.text: Mr Livingstone may do Oriental sport

parts.note: Ken Livingstone is a British politician, a former Mayor of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A London politician might take up a Japanese martial art.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone is a British left-wing politician who was Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is Japanese fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Article impounded by rebel recruit

indicators.note: impounded means shut up in an enclosure, so one piece is penned inside the other

parts.note: to rise is to rebel, as in a rising against the government
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is confiscated by an insurgent signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise troops is to recruit or muster them.

clue.text: Anger caused by odour of sanctity

explanation.surface: Rage is provoked by the smell of holiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to enrage; it is also the fragrant resin burned in churches, giving a holy smell.

clue.text: Dilapidated manse is in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A rundown vicarage needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dilapidated is untidy and disordered, in a muddle.

clue.text: Criminal conclusion fills girls with depression

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: gals is an informal word for girls
a low is a depression, in weather or mood

explanation.surface: An ending makes young women feel downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The structure for hanging was where a condemned criminal's life ended.

clue.text: Useless information about blood group results in resentment

parts.note: a dud is something useless

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
O is a blood group

explanation.surface: Worthless facts on blood types lead to bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to feel indignant resentment.
